findings.current: 制造成本大幅下降、新的计算机芯片让机器运行得更好等多种原因，使机器人近年来进步迅速，它们在日常生活中正发挥着越来越重要的作用。

findings.reason: 用“它”开头接上定语从句，是 which is caused by 的直译，翻译腔明显。改用“这种感受”复指，更符合中文说明文的写法。“比如”仍然紧跟在“某件事”后面，举的是什么事的例子一看就清楚。

The current line matches the file. 'not from just guessing…, but from scientific research': 通过科学研究得出的 is exact and mirrors the first half (仅凭猜测…得出的), which fixes the mismatched 不是…而是 halves. Nothing is lost.

The current line matches the file. Starting a clause with 它 to stand for an abstract noun is a typical translationese marker of 'which'. 这种感受由某件事引起 is equally precise (strong positive feeling caused by an event), and 比如 still follows 某件事, so the examples clearly illustrate the event.

vb.why: 怀有相反的感受 is an awkward collocation (怀有 goes with 希望, 敬意 and similar). 它们的感受可能正好相反 is the natural Chinese. 可能, 实际上 and 情绪低落 are all kept and the meaning is unchanged.
不是……得出的，而是来自…… is unbalanced. The English not from…but from… is parallel, and 不是……得出的，而是通过……得出的 restores that. The meaning is the same.

A clause starting with 它 is a literal copy of the English 'which is caused by'. Restating the noun as 这种感受 is the normal way to do this in Chinese expository writing. The meaning is unchanged and 比如 still follows 某件事.

va.why: The current line matches the file, and the problem is real: 记着 means 'keep in mind', but 'a rush to remember' means hurrying not to forget things. The proposal says 'rush' twice (手忙脚乱 and 急着) and adds 手忙脚乱, which is stronger than 'rush'. 回想 also usually means recalling the past. The amended line keeps every part: feels like = 感觉是在, a rush = 急急忙忙, to remember = 想着别漏带, necessary things like socks or medicine = 必需品，比如袜子或药品.

'might' (modal, 可能会) is a 中考 word, and it is annotated elsewhere in the project (v. 可能（会）). v. （情态动词）可能；也许 is correct for 'They might try folding…' and passes the POS-prefix check.

see sb do (bare infinitive 'put' after 'sees') is a real 中考 point and fits the project's style (ask sb if, allow sb to do, by doing). But the proposal as written breaks the build. Without a {surface}, build.find cannot locate 'see sb do' (returns None). With {sees … put}, 'put' is already taken by the existing put…together entry, so find again returns None (tested) and the result is a 找不到 build error. vb.why: In the current line, 记着 means 'keep in mind', which is the wrong sense for 'a rush to remember', and 感觉像是在匆匆忙忙地… is a word-for-word rendering. 手忙脚乱，急着回想要带哪些必需品 keeps both the rush and the remembering, reads naturally, and the 比如 example still sits right after 必需品.
好让衣服变小一些 can be read as the clothes actually shrinking. 把衣服叠得更小一些 says what the English means. The 把 also matters: the shorter 好叠得更小 could be misread as 'easy to fold'.

might is junior-high vocabulary and is easy to mistake for a plain past form. 可能 in the translation matches it, the project already glosses might as v. 可能（会）, and it does not overlap any other highlight.

understand is junior-high vocabulary and z04 already glosses it in two sentences, so leaving it out here is inconsistent. 理解 matches 开始理解 in the translation, and it does not overlap any other highlight.

findings.reason: “载有”是书面语，多用于船只、文件等（“载有乘客”“载有条款”），用来说卡片不自然，初中生读着也生硬。拆成“准备了……卡片，上面有……”，既口语化，又和正文第6句的“卡片上有著名的诗歌和主题画”一致。

findings.proposed: become=v. 变成；成为
findings.reason: 'it became an amazing trip': become is a core junior-high verb (the past form became is irregular) and has no entry here. z16 [28] annotates become, so this sentence should too.

findings.proposed: both=pron. 两者都；双方都
findings.reason: 'they both benefited greatly': both is a junior-high curriculum word, used here as a pronoun after the subject (the ZH says 双方都). Learners need it, and it has no entry.

findings.proposed: understand=v. 理解；明白
findings.reason: 'help them better understand our poems': understand is a junior-high curriculum verb and has no entry. Easier words such as learn, share and prepare are annotated elsewhere in this passage.

findings.current: 有很多含义；意义重大
findings.proposed: 含义丰富；有很多含义
findings.reason: In this sentence 'Each character means a lot in poems' means each character carries a lot of meaning. 意义重大 is a different sense (mean a lot to sb = 对某人很重要), so it misleads learners about this use.

findings.current: adj. 有趣的
findings.proposed: n. 乐趣；有趣的事
findings.reason: 'learning poems can be fun': here fun is a predicative after be. The 课标 word list and 中考 teaching treat this as the uncountable noun (It's (great) fun ...). The adj. label fits only attributive use, as in 'fun cards' [5] and 'a fun place' [12], where adj. is correct.

findings.current: （倒装句）……上有……
findings.reason: This entry is a free grammatical structure (a place adverbial plus be plus subject, in full inversion), not a fixed phrase, yet it is labelled 短语. The capitalised discontinuous headword 'On…were' is also not a learnable lexical item. The ZH already shows the meaning, and the sentence has five other valid entries.

findings.current: n. 水（汉语拼音）
findings.reason: 'shui' is Chinese pinyin, not English vocabulary. Listing it as an n. entry is pointless and may make learners think it is an English word. The sentence has six other valid entries.

findings.proposed: most=adj. 大多数的
findings.reason: 'For most foreign teenagers': most is used as a determiner meaning 大多数的 (not the superlative 最). This is a junior-high usage and it has no entry.

findings.proposed: could=modal v. 可能
findings.reason: 'learning Chinese poems could be boring': could here means possibility (可能), not the past of can that primary learners know. This junior-high modal sense has no entry.

findings.current: 对大多数外国青少年来说，学习中国诗歌可能很枯燥，但一所中学的中国学生成立了“诗会”社团，帮助在中国的交换生学到更多。
findings.proposed: 对大多数外国青少年来说，学习中国诗歌可能很枯燥，但对一群在中国的交换生来说，这却成了一段奇妙的旅程：一所中学的中国学生成立了“诗会”社团，帮助他们学到更多。
findings.reason: 原文的转折是“对多数外国青少年来说枯燥，但对这群交换生来说成了奇妙的旅程”（[1]-[2]）。概要漏掉了“奇妙的旅程”，让“但”直接接到“成立社团”上，把文章开头的对比关系弄偏了。

va.why: The current text matches the file. 'cards about X' means cards whose theme is X, so '以……为主题的卡片' is exact. It removes the Europeanised '关于……的' attributive and the stacked '的大漠的卡片', and 主题 is glossed in [6].
The substring matches the summary. '载有' is bookish and odd for cards. The proposal says the same content in plainer words that match the ZH of [6]. It does not overlap with the summary change in #18.

become (past form became, irregular) is a junior-high curriculum verb. z16 [28] annotates it, so annotating it here is consistent. v. 变成；成为 is correct for 'it became an amazing trip'. become is in 基础词.txt, so the entry is optional, but it is harmless and useful.
'they both benefited': both is a pronoun used after the subject, which is a junior-high teaching point. pron. 两者都；双方都 is correct and matches the ZH 双方都. The pron. label passes the POS check.
understand is a junior-high curriculum verb that learners must know. v. 理解；明白 is the exact sense in 'better understand our poems' and matches the ZH 理解.

The current gloss matches the file. Here the meaning is 'each character carries a lot of meaning' (see the 水 example and the ZH 有丰富的含义). 意义重大 is the 'is important (to sb)' sense and would mislead learners. The proposed gloss fits this use.

The current gloss matches the file. Predicative 'be fun' is taught in 中考 as the uncountable noun (It's great fun / What fun!). An adj. label invites the error 'very fun'. n. 乐趣；有趣的事 is the standard junior-high analysis, and the attributive uses in [5] and [12] stay adj.

The entry matches the file. 'On…were' is a free full-inversion structure, not a lexical phrase, and the discontinuous capitalised headword is not a learnable item. On and were are basic words, so dropping it causes no 漏标 error, and five valid entries remain.

The current entry already says '（汉语拼音）', so it does not mislead. Dropping it would break the automatic check: ann_lib.uncovered has no exemption for pinyin, and lowercase 'shui' is not a basic word, so check_ann would flag it as a missing annotation.

'For most foreign teenagers': most is a determiner meaning 大多数的, not the superlative 最. That distinction is worth teaching, and it matches the ZH 大多数. adj. is the 课标/Chinese-dictionary label and passes the POS check.

The sense is right: 'could be boring' expresses possibility, a junior-high modal use. But 'modal v.' fails the POS check in ann_lib.py (it requires the gloss to start with n./v./adj./...) and is not used anywhere in the corpus, where might is glossed 'v. 可能（会）'. Use 'v.'.

The substring matches the summary. The draft skips [2] ('it became an amazing trip'), so '但' jumps from 'boring' straight to 'founded a club'. The proposal restores the actual contrast in [1]-[2] precisely and does not overlap with the change in #5.

vb.why: '关于……大漠的卡片' stacks a long modifier and produces two 的 in a row, which is translationese. '以……为主题的卡片' is natural, says exactly what 'cards about' means, and echoes 主题画 in [6].
'载有' is bookish and is used for ships or documents, so it is odd for cards. Splitting the clause into '准备了“趣味卡片”，上面有……' is plainer, keeps the meaning, and matches the ZH of [6].
become (past form became, irregular) is a core junior-high verb. It is unannotated here but annotated in z16 [28]. The sense 成为 fits 'became an amazing trip'.
both is a junior-high curriculum word (taught as pron. 两者都 in 八上). Here it is a pronoun after the subject ('they both'), it matches the ZH 双方都, and it is not annotated anywhere.
understand is a junior-high verb that learners must know. Its highlight overlaps with the 'help sb do' span, but the corpus already allows that (z05 [7], z19 [16]), so the add is safe.

In context (the 水 example that follows), 'means a lot' means each character carries rich meaning. 意义重大 is the different sense 'mean a lot to sb'. A gloss must give only the sense used in this sentence.

The current gloss is accurate. Predicative 'be fun' is widely treated as an adjective, and the 人教版 textbook labels exactly the 'X is fun' use as 'fun adj. 有趣的' (七上 Unit 9). It also matches the ZH 很有趣. Switching to n. is a debatable preference, not a correction.

'On…were' is not a lexical item. It is a free inverted structure mislabelled as 短语, and the capitalised discontinuous headword cannot be learned as vocabulary. The ZH already conveys the meaning, and five valid entries remain.
'shui' is Chinese pinyin, not English vocabulary. Listing it as an English n. entry misleads learners, and six valid entries remain.
most used as a determiner meaning 大多数的 is a junior-high usage, different from the superlative 最. Learners need it and it is unannotated. adj. 大多数的 is the standard Chinese dictionary and 课标 label.

could is among the most common primary-level function words, which the user's rule allows to be left out. No modal verb is annotated anywhere in the corpus (many 'could' sentences, e.g. z17 [17]). The possibility sense is already clear from the ZH 可能, so annotating it adds noise.

The passage contrasts 'boring for most foreign teens' with 'an amazing trip for this group'. The current summary drops the amazing trip and hangs 但 on founding the club, which skews that contrast. The proposal restores it naturally and adds nothing that is not in the text.

findings.current: 毫无疑问，快递服务在我们的生活中既智能，又对环境友好。
findings.proposed: 毫无疑问，我们生活中的快递服务既智能，又对环境友好。
findings.reason: “在我们的生活中”放在主语和形容词谓语“既智能”之间，照搬了英文语序，读着别扭。改为定语“我们生活中的快递服务”更顺，意思不变。

findings.current: 每秒钟都有6,000多件包裹在运送途中。
findings.proposed: 每秒钟都有6000多件包裹在运送途中。
findings.reason: 按 GB/T 15835 的数字用法，一般中文行文里四位数不加千分撇，“6000多件”才合中文书写习惯。

findings.proposed: since=prep. 自……以来
findings.reason: 'Since the 1990s … has also grown' has no entry for 'since'. It is a junior-high word, not a primary-school one, and since + present perfect is a key 中考 grammar point. It is annotated in z19 [21] with the same gloss, so z18 should have it too for consistency.

va.why: The current text matches [23]. '快递服务在我们的生活中既智能' copies the English word order. '我们生活中的快递服务既智能，又对环境友好' keeps every element and reads clearly better.

Not an error. GB/T 15835 only says a four-digit number *may* go without separators. The project's 中考 ZH consistently keeps the thousands comma to mirror the on-screen English: z07 '6,212', z09 '1,872', z25 '1,800', z31 '3,046'. Changing only z18 would create an inconsistency.

In [13], 'Since the 1990s … has also grown' has no entry for since. It is in 基础词, but it is a junior-high curriculum word, and since + present perfect is a core 中考 grammar point. The same batch already annotates it in z19 [21] with this gloss. 'prep. 自……以来' is correct here.

vb.why: 在我们的生活中既智能 copies the odd English 'smart in our life' word order and makes 在生活中 scope awkwardly over both predicates. 我们生活中的快递服务既智能，又对环境友好 is smoother and means effectively the same.

Normal Chinese practice (and GB/T 15835 for general text) writes four-digit numbers without a comma. The same file already writes 5亿多件 and 1800亿件 without separators, so 6000多件 is correct and consistent.

since (prep. 自……以来) is a junior-high curriculum word and a key 中考 point with the present perfect, not a primary-school word. It is unannotated here but annotated in z19 [21]. The rule that every junior-high word must be annotated requires it.

findings.current: 事实上，我们拥有的火星地图比海底地图更好。
findings.proposed: 事实上，我们手里的火星地图比海底地图还要好。
findings.reason: “我们拥有的……更好”是典型的翻译腔（拿“拥有”对译 have）。另外，这句话的要点是一个出人意料的对比：远在天边的火星，地图反而比我们自己的海底地图好，“In fact”在这里正起强调作用。改用“手里的……还要好”，意思不变，读起来更自然，也把这层意外感表达了出来。

findings.current: 一种叫作珊瑚虫的微小动物建造出珊瑚坚硬的部分，把它当作自己居住的家。
findings.proposed: 一种叫作珊瑚虫的微小动物建造出珊瑚坚硬的部分，当作自己的家，住在里面。
findings.reason: “把它当作”多了一个“它”。“居住的家”语义重复，因为“家”本来就是住的地方。改成“当作自己的家，住在里面”更顺，也能看出高亮短语 live in（住在……里）。

findings.current: 自1982年以来，科学家们已经把旧地铁车厢放进了海里。
findings.proposed: 自1982年以来，科学家们已经陆续把旧地铁车厢放进了海里。
findings.reason: 中文“自……以来”后面要接持续或累积的动作。只说“已经把车厢放进了海里”像是做了一次就完事，和“自……以来”对不上。原文 since 加现在完成时、复数 cars，表示多年来不断投放，加“陆续”才准确、自然。

findings.current: 一个典型的例子是L形礁。
findings.proposed: L形礁就是一个典型的例子。
findings.reason: “一个典型的例子是X”照搬了英文 A typical example is X 的语序。中文习惯先说具体事物，再说它是什么，即“L形礁就是一个典型的例子”。

findings.current: 我们对它却知之甚少，探索海洋是一项非常艰难的工作
findings.proposed: 我们对它却知之甚少。探索海洋是一项非常艰难的工作
findings.reason: 概要第一句连用四个逗号，话题从“对海洋知之甚少”换到“探索很难”时没有断开，一逗到底，句子太长。在这里改用句号，层次就清楚了。

findings.proposed: one{ones}=pron. （代替前面提到的名词）……的那些（此处指更小的碎块）
findings.reason: 'break them into even smaller ones' uses 'ones' as a substitute pronoun for 'pieces'. This substitute use of one/ones is a junior-high grammar point, and without an entry learners may not see that 'ones' refers back to the coral pieces.

findings.current: 海洋覆盖了地球的大部分面积，我们对它却知之甚少，探索海洋是一项非常艰难的工作，但许多科学家正在迎接这一挑战，他们最重要的目标之一是了解珊瑚礁。
findings.proposed: 海洋覆盖了地球的大部分面积，我们对它却知之甚少，因为探索海洋是一项非常艰难的工作。但许多科学家正在迎接这一挑战，他们最重要的目标之一是了解珊瑚礁。
findings.reason: In the passage, 'Exploring the ocean is a really hard job' answers 'Why?', so it is the reason we know so little. In the summary's long comma chain that cause is lost, and the clause just sits next to the others. The following 但 then reads as contrasting with the whole run-on. Adding 因为 and breaking the sentence before 但 restores the passage's logic: little known, because exploring is hard, but scientists take on the challenge.

va.why: The current text matches the file. '我们拥有的' is stiff, and '还要好' correctly brings out the surprise in 'In fact … better maps of Mars than … ocean floor'. But '手里的' is too colloquial and suggests holding the maps in your hand. Simply saying '我们的火星地图' is precise and natural.
va.amended_proposed: 事实上，我们的火星地图比海底地图还要好。

va.why: The current text matches [11]. '居住的家' is redundant. '当作自己的家，住在里面' fully covers 'as a home to live in' with nothing lost, reads more naturally and lines up with the highlighted 'live in'.

The current text matches [21]. 'Since 1982' with present-perfect 'have placed' and plural 'cars' describes placing that has gone on over many years. '陆续' makes this explicit and removes the mismatch between '自……以来' and a seemingly one-off action. It is precise and more natural.

'一个典型的例子是L形礁' is normal, idiomatic Chinese. It is not translationese. Keeping the new information 'L形礁' at the end also leads naturally into [21], which goes on to describe this reef. The rewrite is not clearly more natural.

This edits the same stretch of the z19 summary as index 13, so applying both would conflict. Index 13 fixes the same run-on and also restores the passage's cause ('Why? Exploring the ocean is a really hard job'), so it is accepted instead.

Worth adding: in [17], the substitute 'ones' in 'even smaller ones' is a junior-high grammar point. The proposed note is imprecise, though: 'ones' replaces only 'pieces', not 'smaller pieces' ('smaller' is a separate adjective). The gloss should name what it replaces.
va.amended_proposed: one{ones}=pron. （代替前面提到的复数名词，此处代替 pieces）……的那些

va.why: The current text matches the z19 summary. In the passage, 'Why? Exploring the ocean is a really hard job' gives the reason we know little. Adding '因为' and breaking before '但' restores that logic and ends the comma chain. Every fact is kept. This supersedes index 8.

vb.why: Using 拥有的 for 'have' is translationese. 手里的…还要好 means the same thing, reads naturally to a 14-year-old, and 还要 captures the surprising Mars-versus-ocean-floor contrast. No change in meaning.
居住的家 is redundant. 当作自己的家，住在里面 reads smoothly, keeps 'as a home to live in' complete, and makes the highlighted live in visible. No meaning lost.

自…以来 needs an ongoing or cumulative predicate. 已经把车厢放进了海里 on its own sounds like a single completed act. 陆续 accurately renders since + present perfect with plural cars (placed over many years) and fixes the awkward collocation.

一个典型的例子是L形礁 is a fully standard, natural Chinese structure. It also puts the new information (L形礁) last, which suits the flow into the next sentences about the subway cars. The rewrite is a matter of taste only.

It edits the same span as #13, and #13 is better: #13 breaks the comma chain before 但 and also restores the passage's cause (little known because exploring is hard). Applying both would conflict, so #13 should be used instead.

vb.amended_proposed: one{ones}=pron. （代替前面提到的复数名词）……的那些（此处代替 pieces，指碎块）
vb.why: Junior-high learners do need to learn ones as a substitute for a noun, so adding it is right. But the proposed note 此处指更小的碎块 wrongly folds 'smaller' into ones. ones replaces only pieces (碎块), and 更小的 comes from smaller. The gloss should say exactly what ones stands for.

In the passage, 'Exploring the ocean is a really hard job' is the answer to 'Why?', so adding 因为 is faithful. Breaking the sentence before 但 ends the four-comma chain, and 这一挑战 still clearly refers back to the hard job. This replaces #8.

findings.current: 这有助于让清理海洋的工作高效得多，因为船只可以被派到正确的地点，迅速收集塑料垃圾。
findings.proposed: 这有助于让清理海洋的工作高效得多，因为可以把船只派到合适的地点，迅速收集塑料垃圾。
findings.reason: 英文用的是被动语态 can be sent，直译成“可以被派到”带翻译腔，中文习惯说“可以把船只派到”。the right places 指的是该去的、对的地方，译成“合适的地点”比“正确的地点”更地道，而且与释义“正确的；合适的”一致。

findings.current: 单个调整都不大，但所有调整加在一起，就能产生很大的作用。
findings.proposed: 单看每一项调整都不大，但所有调整合在一起，就能起到很大的作用。
findings.reason: “单个……都”搭配不当：“单个”指一个，“都”指全部，读起来别扭，“No single change is big”应译为“单看每一项调整都不大”。“产生……作用”也不如“起到……作用”自然。“合在一起”还和 together 的释义一致。

findings.current: make…change
findings.proposed: make changes
findings.reason: 'make…change' is not a real dictionary form: without an article the citation is ungrammatical. The fixed collocation is 'make a change / make changes'. The sentence has the plural, 'makes … changes', so the entry should read '~make changes{makes…changes}=做出改变；进行调整'. In the same file, [21] already uses the proper form 'make a choice'. The current gloss also mixes 做出 and 作出 within one line; use one form consistently.

findings.proposed: ~a month=每月；每个月
findings.reason: 'dropped from 19 a month to zero': here 'a' means 'per' (每), which is a sense learners do not get from the basic article. The ZH says 每月19起, but nothing in the vocabulary list explains where 每月 comes from.

va.why: The current text matches [18]. '可以被派到' is translationese. '可以把船只派到合适的地点' keeps every clause ('the ships', 'can be sent', 'the right places', 'collect … quickly'), reads more naturally and matches the gloss for 'right'.

The current text matches [8]. The '单个……都' pairing is awkward. '单看每一项调整都不大' precisely renders 'No single change is big', '合在一起' matches the gloss for 'together', and '起到很大的作用' fits 'make a big difference' and its gloss.

The headword matches [7]. 'make…change' with no article is not a citation form, and 'make change' actually means 'give change for money'. 'make changes' is a real collocation that matches the highlighted 'makes … changes' and follows [21]'s 'make a choice' convention. Also apply the gloss fix from the reason (做出改变；进行调整, using 做出 consistently).

Real gap: in [13], '19 a month' uses a in the sense of 'per' (每), and the ZH '每月' is not explained anywhere in the list. But a bare 'a month = 每月' could teach learners that 'a month' always means 每月, when it usually means 一个月. The gloss should say that a means 每 here.
va.amended_proposed: ~a month=（a 表示“每”）每月；每个月

vb.why: 可以被派到 is a stiff copy of the English passive; 可以把船只派到 is the normal Chinese structure. 合适的地点 fits 'the right places' (where the plastic is) better than 正确的地点 and is still covered by the gloss 正确的；合适的. The meaning is unchanged.

单个…都 is an ill-formed pairing (one vs. all). 单看每一项调整都不大 renders 'No single change is big' correctly and idiomatically. 起到很大的作用 is the standard collocation and matches the gloss 起（很大）作用, and 合在一起 matches the gloss for together.

make…change is not a proper citation form; without an article or plural it is ungrammatical. make changes fits the plural in the sentence and is standard. When applying, also make the gloss's 做出/作出 consistent, e.g. 做出改变；做出调整 (or 进行调整), to match the ZH 做出…小调整.

Using a to mean 'per' (once a week, 19 a month) is taught in junior high, and learners otherwise cannot see where 每月 in the ZH comes from. The phrase a month = 每月；每个月 is accurate and appears only once in the sentence.
